_comment: Shared golden vectors for the sealed-preferences byte layout. Loaded by BOTH
suites: SealedBlobVectorTest.kt drives KeystoreSecretStore.openWithKey with a
software AES key, SealedBlobVectorTest.swift drives CryptoKit's AES.GCM.open
over SealedBox(combined:). The layout is nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16),
the claim docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md makes under 'Insufficient cryptography'.
Neither side can inject a nonce into its SEALING path (Android's provider
chooses the IV), so the vectors pin the OPENING direction: a fixed key and a
fixed blob must open to the same plaintext on both platforms. Whatever one
side seals, the other must therefore be able to open. A sealing change that
kept the round-trip but altered the layout would turn the other suite red.
The blobs were produced by an independent AES-256-GCM implementation, not
by either port. All byte strings are lower-case hex. 'expected' is the UTF-8
plaintext; 'expectFailure' true means the tag must NOT authenticate.

open.description: a small JSON document opens to its plaintext
an empty plaintext is nonce plus tag alone, 28 bytes
one flipped bit in the tag fails authentication
a blob shorter than a nonce plus a tag is rejected
